To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the free radicals formed from the addition of OH radicals to phenol, cresols and 4-ethylphenol, undergo unimolecular decomposition with a rate constant of about 2 X 10 ^{8} sec.-1.

the unimolecular elimination reactions of OH addition radicals to hydroxybenzenes, and to other aromatic compounds, proceed with rate constants in the range 10^5-10^7 s^−1 and with activation energies of 0.1–0.5 eV, that the reactions proceed with a change in the aromatic ring, that the reaction is not a simple elimination of the hydroxybenzene, and that the reaction is probably a rearrangement reaction of the hydroxy

the OH adducts of the hydroxybenzenes, 1,2- and 1,3-dihydroxybenzenes and catechol, are formed in the radiolysis of aqueous solutions of these compounds, that they decompose by unimolecular elimination reactions, and that the rates of decomposition are dependent on the nature of the hydroxy substituent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reactions of OH addition to hydroxybenzenes, the reactions of OH radicals with the resulting hydroxycyclohexadienyl radicals, and the unimolecular decomposition of these latter radicals.

the reactions of OH addition to the aromatic ring in the free radicals produced by the pulse radiolysis of hydroxybenzenes, and with the subsequent unimolecular eliminations of the OH group from these adduct free radicals.
the unimolecular elimination of hydrogen halide and hydrogen sulphide from free radicals produced by the addition of OH to halogeno- and sulphonated hydroxybenzenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unimolecular free-radical elimination reactions are not only possible but are of general occurrence.
, in the case of hydroxybenzenes, OH addition to the aromatic ring is followed by the unimolecular elimination reaction: R-OH + R'OH + O2 + H2O.
, in the free radicals produced by addition of the OH radical to the hydroxybenzenes, the C-O bond is cleaved to give a phenoxyl radical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OH radical adds to the aromatic ring in hydroxybenzenes to form a free radical which undergoes a unimolecular decomposition to a phenol, CO, and an alkoxy radical.
the OH radical addition to the hydroxybenzenes is followed by a rapid unimolecular elimination to give a phenoxyl free radical.

, in the case of the OH-addition free radicals of phenols, the unimolecular decomposition reaction is the major reaction in the absence of a hydrogen donor and is the dominant reaction when a hydrogen donor is present.
